interface.title: Arp Catalog · iTelescope Project (arp_project.html)
interface.field: Observational astronomy: amateur and pro-am deep-sky imaging of peculiar galaxies on remote iTelescope telescopes
interface.stage_of_work: Planning observations, logging sessions, and tracking progress across a multi-season imaging survey
interface.what_it_is_for: A single-page dashboard for planning which of the 338 Arp galaxies to image each night at an iTelescope site (visibility window, moon risk, cost), writing ACP plan files for the scheduled targets, logging each session with a quality rating, and tracking survey completion and the re-image queue. Season-level batch ACP generation and moon-data refresh are separate Python-script stages of the project and are not part of this page.

data.note: The 338-target Arp catalogue (season, size, telescope and filter suggestions) is built into the page. NED coordinates load automatically from arp_ned_coords.csv on the server (header shows 'Coords: NED (338)'). The moon calendar (Overview strip, Moon calendar tab) is precomputed data covering 2026-04-15 onward, and the header 'Moon: 7%' comes from it. It does not follow today's date (2026-11-01). Tonight's plan works out moon illumination and separation for the chosen date itself: 55% on 2026-11-01 and 99.6% on 2026-11-24. Status and log are kept in browser localStorage and survived a reload (screens/029.webp).

tree.general: Plan, carry out and track a multi-season imaging survey of a fixed target catalogue
tree.specific: Image all 338 Arp galaxies on iTelescope telescopes, avoiding the moon and keeping track of quality and completion. Season-level batch ACP generation and refreshing the moon data are done with the repository's Python scripts, outside this page

Regenerating ACP plans or moon data with the repository's Python scripts: no shell is available. Season-level batch ACP generation and moon-data refresh are script-only stages outside this page. As a result the moon calendar stays on its precomputed April–June 2026 range and does not follow the current date.
Clicking a heatmap cell or a bar in the Moon calendar did not drill down. A heatmap cell's hover text is only 'G', 'M' or 'A'.
Possible issue: Export ACP target list wrote arp_remaining_all.txt containing the remaining targets even when 'Re-image queue' was selected, so it seems to ignore the status selector.
Possible issue: logging a 4★ re-image of Arp 319 did not remove its earlier 2★ entry from the re-image candidates. The queue only cleared when the 2★ entry was deleted.
The 'Download all (2 files)' click gave only the first file at first. The second file (Arp319-T5-20261101.txt) arrived a moment later.
